rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient to observe all 10 compounds and identify the elution window and limiting pairs. The moderate temperature leaves room to adjust selectivity in either direction while targeting a short run.

Change only gradient duration to test whether the two limiting pairs respond to a shallower slope. The current last peak at 7.16 minutes leaves room to improve resolution while likely keeping all peaks within 10 minutes.

The limiting pair improved strongly with a shallower gradient. Raising phi0 to 0.15 at the same duration further reduces the slope while removing low-organic time, aiming for full resolution with the last peak still below 10 minutes.

Lengthen the trimmed gradient by two minutes to increase resolution of the sole limiting pair. Based on the previous slope response and the current 8.62-minute last peak, this could achieve R ≥ 1.5 throughout while keeping the last peak below 10 minutes.
Injection 4 reached the maximum possible CRF, so retain it as the benchmark. Increase only temperature to test whether all peaks can elute sooner while preserving full resolution and CRF 1.000.

Test whether a larger temperature shift carries the limiting pair through its apparent selectivity crossover and restores separation with a shorter gradient. Injection 4 remains the maximum-score fallback; this run will also check for new limiting pairs at higher temperature.

Lengthen only the gradient to test whether the new limiting pair at 55 C reaches full resolution. The last peak at 7.71 minutes leaves ample room for this adjustment to match CRF 1.000 while eluting sooner than injection 4.

Slightly narrow the gradient window to improve the limiting pair from R 1.41 to an estimated R above 1.5. The last peak should remain inside the gradient and below 10 minutes, potentially matching the maximum CRF with earlier elution than injection 4.

Shift both gradient endpoints upward by 0.05, preserving the slope of injection 8 while testing whether the fully resolved separation can finish sooner. Monitor the early peaks for excessive loss of retention and the two closest pairs for selectivity changes.

The higher starting organic fraction substantially worsened the limiting pair, so test a lower phi0 with the shorter 14-minute gradient. This may restore full resolution while keeping the last peak earlier than injection 8; monitor the other close pair for any loss of separation.

Injection 10 achieved the maximum CRF with the earliest fully resolved last peak so far. Shorten only the gradient to test whether its two closest pairs retain R ≥ 1.5 at a still shorter elution time.

Reduce the endpoint to make the 12-minute gradient shallower, targeting R ≥ 1.5 for the sole unresolved pair. This slope lies between injections 11 and 10 and should preserve the other close pair while finishing slightly earlier than injection 10.

Use a slightly steeper gradient than injection 12, intermediate between the successful and unsuccessful slopes tested at 55 C. This targets full resolution with the last peak around 7.8 minutes, while the endpoint remains above the observed elution window.

The maximum CRF is already secured; test a substantially cooler temperature for an alternative selectivity window that could support a shorter fully resolved separation. The broad, steep gradient limits the added retention at low temperature, while injection 13 remains the fastest maximum-score method observed.

Return to the successful 55 C selectivity window and lower phi0 relative to injection 11 to test whether the limiting pair improves despite the slightly steeper slope. This could retain full resolution with the last peak earlier than injection 13; maximum-score methods remain available as fallbacks.

Test the upper temperature limit with a steeper gradient to seek a faster, fully resolved separation beyond the selectivity crossover seen near 55 C. Injection 15 already secures CRF 1.000; this exploratory run checks whether reordered middle peaks can resolve at a shorter elution time.

The middle pair appears to have reversed order at 60 C; a higher starting organic fraction and steeper gradient may separate it further on this side of the crossover. Test this faster method while checking that the early peaks and remaining middle pairs retain adequate resolution.

Shorten only the gradient to determine whether the reversed middle pair gains further resolution with increasing steepness at 60 C. Monitor the neighboring pair, currently R 1.62, for compression; injection 15 remains the fastest verified maximum-score fallback.

Test the unexplored 35 C selectivity window with a moderate gradient, seeking full resolution at a shorter elution time than injection 15. The steep-gradient trials at 60 C introduced competing resolution losses, so retain the verified CRF 1.000 methods as fallbacks.

Test the unexplored 50 C selectivity window with a short gradient, using low starting organic to preserve early retention. This probes whether temperature and slope can jointly resolve the middle cluster faster than the verified 7.60-minute maximum-score separation.

Test a modestly steeper slope than injection 15 at the same starting composition and temperature to locate the shortest fully resolved boundary. The endpoint remains above the last peak’s estimated elution composition, but the two closest pairs must retain R ≥ 1.5 to match the maximum CRF.

Preserve injection 15’s successful slope and temperature while trimming the gradient endpoint above the last peak’s estimated elution composition of 0.57. This should retain CRF 1.000 and the 7.60-minute last peak with a shorter programmed gradient.

Test the next steeper grid slope beyond injection 13 to refine the shortest fully resolved boundary at this starting composition. The limiting pair is predicted to be near R 1.5, while injection 22 remains the verified maximum-score fallback.

Preserve injection 12’s fully resolving slope while trimming the endpoint to just above the last peak’s estimated elution composition of 0.56. This should retain CRF 1.000 and its slightly larger minimum-resolution margin with an eight-minute programmed gradient.

Use the proven 0.075-per-minute slope at 55 C with an intermediate endpoint, expected to preserve full resolution and the 7.60-minute last peak. This final variant targets CRF 1.000 while providing a stronger final solvent than injection 22 and a shorter programmed gradient than injection 15.
